name: pal
description: Deterministic OS surface, bump allocator, FP-free stdio
note: Platform-specific wraps are in the platform packages: the ZisK accelerator arenas and inline_bump_alloc_aligned (whose __wrap_ definitions are here, in module.c) in libziskos.bflat.manifest of bflat-libziskos; the SP1 and OpenVM memory primitives and SP1's main in the platform manifests of bflat-sp1 and bflat-openvm, whose entry.S defines them.

wrap.note: Process/environment identity stubs for the OS-less guest; getenv is the config tunnel (invariant globalization & co).
The downward bump allocator - the only memory in the guest.

Aligned allocation: musl's aligned_alloc/memalign walk mallocng chunk metadata the bump heap never writes, so route them through the bump allocator too (SystemNative_AlignedAlloc is the runtime-startup caller).
No threads, no signals, no time, no syscall passthrough oddities.
The real PalGetMaximumStackBounds aborts under static musl on RISC-V (mremap EINVAL); report a synthetic 8 MiB window instead.
FP-free vfprintf: keeps musl's fmt_fp float formatter out of the link.

musl's scanf/float-parsing members (vfscanf.o, floatscan.o, fmodl.o) are the only libc.a members with real F/D instructions in the stock hard-float Alpine build, and ziskemu rejects any FP in .text regardless of reachability. Redirecting every reference keeps those members out of the link entirely.
musl exit()/_Exit()/abort() issue exit_group (syscall 94), which ZisK does not treat as program end; emit the real ZisK exit ecall (a7=93).

Hide musl's stdio write path on the real zkVMs; the sim keeps host stdio. The unwrapped one issues a raw writev - harmless on ZisK, which emulates Linux syscalls, but a hard error on SP1 (unknown syscall id) and unserviced on OpenVM, which has no ecall handler at all. Managed console output does not go through it anyway: it takes the SystemNative_Write wrap in rhp, so nothing is lost.
